title: King Street — March 5, 1770
design_note: Built strictly from Rex v. Preston / Rex v. Wemms testimony. The scene never shows who said 'Fire' — the sources genuinely disagree, and honoring that ambiguity IS the scene (docs/05). Natural light: moon, snow, one sentry lantern.

events.note: wind, harbor ice, a dog far off
one redcoat, one lantern, falling snow
boys first, then men; snowballs, oyster shells, a thrown club later sworn to in court
bells ring 'fire' into the night — the town thinks there is a blaze; the ambiguity is the scene
seven privates and a captain, bayonets level, walking INTO the crowd to reach the sentry
per testimony: knocked down by the club, rises, fires first — no order shown, none proven
seven seconds of smoke and silence before anyone understands
Crispus Attucks dead in the snow; no music

events.text: Facts are stubborn things; and whatever may be our wishes, our inclinations, or the dictates of our passions, they cannot alter the state of facts and evidence.
events.attribution: John Adams — for the defense, Rex v. Wemms, 1770

events.text: The game announces its ethic in scene one: this will not be propaganda.
